transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia, Marco (Redwood); Nina, Ethan, Priya (Corvus)

Auto-generated Summary (may be incomplete):
- Procurement and legal alignment on MSA/DPA items, SLA expectations, and next steps for vendor gating.

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, want to be mindful of time — we've got about 45 minutes. I'm Sofia, AE on the account, and Marco is our SE.
[00:12] Nina Huang: Thanks, Sofia. I'm Nina, head of procurement. We'll keep this tight. Priya is on for legal and Ethan is our security lead.
[00:20] Marco Ruiz: Great, quick agenda — go over the MSA/DPA redline expectations, discuss SLA and dedicated capacity options, and then KMS/SSO requirements for private deployment.
[00:32] Priya Kapoor: Quick note, we have a procurement committee on the 2nd of September, so we ideally want legal redlines in by the end of August.
[00:40] Sofia Patel: Understood, we'll aim to get annotated MSA to you by Monday the 24th.
[00:45] Ethan Cole: For security, the key things are: we need KMS integration, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and the ability to enforce retention windows. Also, SOC 2 and ISO artifacts please.
[01:00] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence; I'll upload those. On KMS, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via bring-your-own-key integrations — there's a separate flow for hosted.
[01:18] Nina Huang: On pricing, procurement wants clarity on committed capacity discounts and what counts as billable tokens for dedup/kv cache.
[01:30] Sofia Patel: Right — committed Dedicated pools have a baseline monthly commit and predictable throughput; token billing differences are documented but we'll send a short spreadsheet mapping typical workloads to expected token cost.
[01:45] Priya Kapoor: On the DPA, two items: data residency constraint — we can't allow export outside EU for some data classes — and minimum retention periods for logs.
[01:58] Marco Ruiz: For residency, we have region pinning for Private and can do EU-only hosting for the hosted offering within our EU cluster. For logs, we can configure retention but need to check the exact retention SLAs for audit logs exported.
[02:14] Ethan Cole: There was a term in the MSA draft about "KV cache" — the doc transcribed it as "K V cash" — can you clarify what that implies for our data? Is cached prompt prefixes persisted beyond session?
[02:28] Marco Ruiz: Good catch — KV cache is stored in ephemeral storage tied to the instance; by default it's not persisted beyond the commit unless you request long-term cache. We'll include an explicit line: ephemeral caching for latency unless explicit long-term storage is enabled.
[02:40] Nina Huang: Procurement cares if the vendor can accept standard MSA with our minimal redlines or if enterprise exceptions (insurance, indemnity caps) trigger a commercial review.
[02:52] Sofia Patel: Typically we accept a subset of minimal redlines; material changes to indemnity or subrogation often need legal escalation. We can pre-flag any items that require C-suite signoff.
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: What about SLA credits — can you walk us through typical SLAs and crediting? Specifically for latency and uptime across Dedicated pools.
[03:16] Marco Ruiz: Our Dedicated offering has an uptime SLA and a latency SLO band; credits are scaled based on sustained breaches. For latency we usually define p95 thresholds per route and there are layered fallbacks — if one pool is overloaded we can route to a compatibility variant with slightly higher latency. Credits apply if we miss uptime targets, not micro-latency misses unless they're systemic.
[03:40] Ethan Cole: We need clarity on the "compatibility variant" — is that a quantized model, or a smaller architecture that might degrade quality?
[03:50] Marco Ruiz: It's typically a smaller model variant or different quantization profile; quality impact depends on your prompts. We can run an eval on your sample prompts to quantify delta.
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: Also want to confirm data processing obligations: will Redwood act as a processor under the DPA?
[04:12] Sofia Patel: Yes, we operate as a processor; the DPA will reflect standard processing terms. We often accept customer additions for essential security controls, but some clauses around liability limits are negotiated.
[04:26] Nina Huang: Procurement needs to know what documents we will receive for our packet. List them out please.
[04:34] Marco Ruiz: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 scope summary, encryption architecture, KMS flow diagram (for Private), sample runbook for incident response, data flow diagram — I'll bundle those.
[04:46] Sofia Patel: And we'll include a short pricing attachment showing committed vs on-demand costs with an example workload.
[04:53] Priya Kapoor: For the DPA, can Redwood accept certain EU SCCs or do you require addendum?
[05:00] Marco Ruiz: We use modern data transfer addenda; we can accept EU SCCs where applicable — we'll confirm exact language.
[05:08] Ethan Cole: On the topic of SSO, we require SAML-based SSO with SCIM for provisioning, role-based access control integrated with our IdP, and audit logs forwarded. Any blockers?
[05:22] Marco Ruiz: We support SAML with SCIM provisioning and map roles into RBAC. Audit logs can be exported to S3 or to your SIEM via syslog depending on region. For Private we can also set up direct log streaming.
[05:36] Nina Huang: Another procurement question: do you do background vendor risk assessments? We need an evidence pack for our vendor risk system.
[05:43] Sofia Patel: We can provide the evidence pack — SOC 2, pen test summary redacted, and an attestation letter. We also have a vendor questionnaire template that many customers fill out.
[05:55] Priya Kapoor: For the insurance clause, our standard requires $10M general liability; I saw in the MSA your limit is lower — is that something you can change?
[06:05] Sofia Patel: Insurance limits can be discussed; materially higher caps sometimes require procurement to escalate. We can surface that in the MSA redlines to see if it's acceptable.
[06:18] Ethan Cole: We also need a statement about encrypted at rest and in transit — but more importantly, about key custody: customer-owned keys for Private; hosted keys for the hosted offering. Any audit about who holds keys?
[06:30] Marco Ruiz: Correct — for Private/Dedicated you can bring your own key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS. For hosted, we manage keys but can offer envelope encryption with customer KMS in some enterprise engagements. We'll document the options.
[06:46] Nina Huang: Procurement asks if Redwood will accept a clause for right-to-audit by a third party under NDA.
[06:55] Priya Kapoor: Yes it's common.
[06:58] Sofia Patel: We accept third-party audits with an appropriate schedule and scoping; usually within business hours and limited frequency. We'll flag that in the redline.
[07:10] Marco Ruiz: Quick tech note — if you plan to route PII/data classified workloads to the service, we recommend Private deployment in your region to reduce surface area.
[07:20] Ethan Cole: Agreed. We'll prioritize Private for regulated workloads.
[07:26] Nina Huang: On the procurement timeline — we need final legal signoff before Sep 2 committee, ideally by Aug 28. Can you commit to that cadence?
[07:34] Sofia Patel: We'll aim to. Sofia: (aside) depends on the scale of redlines, but we can often return an annotated MSA within 3 business days.
[07:44] Priya Kapoor: If we get the annotated MSA and a redline back, do we have a point person at Redwood legal?
[07:51] Sofia Patel: I'll introduce you to our legal counsel — name is Aaron Weiss — in the follow-up email.
[07:58] Marco Ruiz: Another operational piece — if you do Dedicated with reserved capacity, we can configure autoscaling vs hard caps. Does procurement need that spelled out?
[08:07] Nina Huang: Yes, for cost forecasting we need predictable spend and clear triggers for auto-scale to avoid surprise bills.
[08:15] Marco Ruiz: We'll include an autoscale policy doc and default thresholds.
[08:20] Ethan Cole: Also, how do you handle data deletion requests — both for customer content and audit logs? We need guaranteed purge windows.
[08:29] Marco Ruiz: We provide documented data deletion flows; for hosted there's a standard purge workflow within X days, Private you can control local retention. We'll confirm exact purge SLAs per artifact type.
[08:40] Priya Kapoor: For the indemnity clause, what's Redwood's standard cap?
[08:44] Sofia Patel: Standard cap is typically tied to the fees paid in prior 12 months, but we can discuss a fixed cap for enterprise deals.
[08:53] Nina Huang: Can you send an initial pricing exhibit that includes committed Dedicated pricing and any lift for BYOK and extended retention?
[08:59] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll include those line items and one example scenario.
[09:05] Priya Kapoor: Procurement also wants to understand the approval path — is this a single-contract signature or do we need multiple sign-offs for network and security?
[09:14] Nina Huang: At Corvus, we need procurement + security + legal signatures; finance signs after commercial terms are confirmed.
[09:22] Sofia Patel: Got it. We'll include a short "what's in the packet" checklist targeted for procurement, security, and legal.
[09:30] Marco Ruiz: One more technical ask — we can do a non-prod benchmark on your sample workload to report latency distributions; would Ethan want that?
[09:37] Ethan Cole: Yes please, send an evaluation harness and we'll provide sample prompts and trace load.
[09:43] Sofia Patel: Great — recap of immediate next steps: Sofia to send annotated MSA by Aug 24; Marco to post SOC2/ISO and KMS diagram by Aug 21; Priya to share DPA mandatory clauses by Aug 22; Nina to confirm procurement committee date by Aug 26.
[09:58] Priya Kapoor: We also want to schedule a runbook/technical deep dive with Marco and Ethan — slot next week?
[10:06] Marco Ruiz: I'm available Wednesday or Thursday afternoon PT.
[10:10] Nina Huang: Let's tentatively plan Thursday at 14:00 PT. I'll confirm.
[10:15] Sofia Patel: Perfect. Anything else before we close?
[10:19] Ethan Cole: One last thing: do you have any known customers in our space (fintech) we can reference for procurement?
[10:28] Sofia Patel: We have a couple of financial services customers, I'll include anonymized references and case studies.
[10:34] Priya Kapoor: Thanks.
[10:36] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifact bundle and redlines.
[10:40] Nina Huang: Appreciate it.

Auto-generated Action Items (may be duplicated above):

End of call.
